title: Financial Mathematics
summary: This unit applies compound interest to real money decisions: perpetuities, sinking funds, bond valuation, EMIs, rates of return including CAGR, and straight-line depreciation. It carries the joint-highest weightage in the paper.

notes.heading: Basics: compound interest and effective rate
notes.html:
• Amount: A = P(1 + i)n, where i = rate per period and n = number of periods. For a nominal rate r compounded m times a year, i = r/m and n = m × years.
  • Present value: PV = A(1 + i)−n.
  • Effective rate = (1 + r/m)m − 1. Example: 8% compounded half-yearly gives (1.04)2 − 1 = 0.0816 = 8.16%.
  • An annuity is a series of equal payments at equal intervals. Ordinary annuity: payments at the end of each period. Annuity due: at the beginning.

notes.heading: Perpetuity
notes.html:
A perpetuity is an annuity whose payments continue forever (e.g. a scholarship fund).

  • Payments at the end of each period: PV = R/i.
  • Payments at the beginning of each period: PV = R + R/i.

Example 1

Find the present value of a perpetuity of ₹6,000 payable at the end of each quarter if money is worth 8% p.a. compounded quarterly.

i = 0.08/4 = 0.02. PV = 6000/0.02 = ₹3,00,000.

notes.heading: Sinking fund
notes.html:
A sinking fund is built by equal periodic deposits to meet a known future liability (replace a machine, redeem debentures).

A = R[(1 + i)n − 1]/i, so R = A·i/[(1 + i)n − 1].

Example 2

A company needs ₹5,00,000 after 10 years. Find the annual deposit at 6% p.a. Given (1.06)10 = 1.7908.

R = 500000 × 0.06/(1.7908 − 1) = 30000/0.7908 ≈ ₹37,936.

notes.heading: EMI: flat rate and reducing balance
notes.html:
• Flat rate: interest is charged on the full principal for the whole term. EMI = (P + P·r·t)/n, with n = number of instalments.
  • Reducing balance: interest is charged on the outstanding balance. EMI = P·i(1 + i)n/[(1 + i)n − 1], with i = monthly rate.

Example 3 (flat)

₹1,20,000 at 10% p.a. flat for 2 years: interest = 120000 × 0.10 × 2 = 24,000. EMI = 144000/24 = ₹6,000.

Example 4 (reducing)

₹5,00,000 at 12% p.a. for 2 years, monthly. i = 0.01, n = 24, (1.01)24 = 1.2697.

EMI = 500000 × 0.01 × 1.2697/0.2697 = 6348.5/0.2697 ≈ ₹23,539.

Each EMI has an interest part (i × outstanding balance) and a principal part (EMI − interest); the interest part falls every month.

notes.heading: Valuation of bonds
notes.html:
A bond pays a fixed periodic interest (coupon) and its face value at maturity. Its fair price is the present value of all these cash flows at the investor's required yield.

PV = C[1 − (1 + i)−n]/i + F(1 + i)−n, where C = coupon per period, F = redemption value, i = yield per period.

Example 5

Face value ₹1,000, coupon 8% p.a. annual, 3 years to maturity, required yield 10%. (1.1)−3 = 0.7513.

PV = 80 × (1 − 0.7513)/0.1 + 1000 × 0.7513 = 80 × 2.487 + 751.3 = 198.96 + 751.3 ≈ ₹950.26.

  • Yield > coupon rate → bond sells at a discount (below face value).
  • Yield < coupon rate → bond sells at a premium.
  • Yield = coupon rate → bond sells at par.

notes.heading: Rate of return and CAGR
notes.html:
• Rate of return = (current value − original value + income received)/original value × 100.
  • CAGR = (EV/BV)1/n − 1, where EV = end value, BV = beginning value, n = number of years. It is the steady yearly growth rate that takes BV to EV.

Example 6

An investment of ₹10,000 becomes ₹14,641 in 4 years. CAGR = (1.4641)1/4 − 1 = 1.1 − 1 = 10%.

Example 7

Shares bought for ₹20,000 are sold for ₹22,500 after receiving ₹500 dividend. Return = (22500 − 20000 + 500)/20000 = 15%.

notes.heading: Depreciation: linear method
notes.html:
Under the straight-line method the asset loses the same amount every year.

Annual depreciation D = (C − S)/n, where C = cost, S = scrap value, n = useful life. Book value after k years = C − kD.

Example 8

Machine cost ₹5,00,000, scrap value ₹50,000, life 9 years. D = 450000/9 = ₹50,000 a year. Book value after 4 years = 500000 − 200000 = ₹3,00,000.

Common mistakes: using the annual rate where a monthly rate is needed; forgetting scrap value; using years instead of number of instalments for n.

keyTerms.definition: An annuity whose payments continue indefinitely.
A fund accumulated by regular equal deposits to meet a future obligation.
Equated monthly instalment: a fixed monthly payment covering interest and principal.
The fixed rate of interest paid on the face value of a bond.
The rate of return an investor earns by holding a bond till maturity.
Compound annual growth rate: the constant annual rate at which an investment grows from its beginning to its end value.
The annual rate actually earned when interest is compounded more than once a year.
The estimated value of an asset at the end of its useful life.

mcqs.q:
Assertion (A): For the same loan, rate and tenure, the flat-rate EMI is higher than the reducing-balance EMI.
Reason (R): Under the flat-rate method, interest is charged on the full principal throughout.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Interest on the full principal, even after part is repaid, makes total interest and hence the EMI larger.

questions.answerHtml: A sinking fund is a fund created by setting aside equal amounts at regular intervals, which with compound interest accumulate to a required sum on a future date.

questions.q: At what rate of interest will the present value of a perpetuity of ₹1,500 payable at the end of every 6 months be ₹40,000?
questions.answerHtml:
PV = R/i → 40000 = 1500/i → i = 0.0375 per half-year.

Annual rate = 2 × 3.75% = 7.5% p.a. compounded half-yearly.

questions.q: A firm wants ₹10,00,000 after 5 years to replace a machine. How much should it deposit at the end of each year in a sinking fund earning 8% p.a.? Given (1.08)<sup>5</sup> = 1.4693.
Find the purchase price of a ₹1,000 bond with a 10% annual coupon redeemable at par after 4 years, if the required yield is 8%. Given (1.08)<sup>−4</sup> = 0.7350.
questions.answerHtml:
C = 100, F = 1000, i = 0.08, n = 4.

Annuity factor = (1 − 0.7350)/0.08 = 3.3125.

PV = 100 × 3.3125 + 1000 × 0.7350 = 331.25 + 735 = ₹1,066.25.

The bond sells at a premium because the coupon rate (10%) exceeds the yield (8%).
